description: The bar chart illustrates five distinct distribution patterns—labeled “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck”—each represented by a set of four light green rectangular bars arranged horizontally along a common baseline, with no numerical axis or scale provided. In the “Increasing” pattern, bar heights rise progressively from left to right, starting with the shortest bar on the far left and ending with the tallest on the far right. The “Uniform” pattern shows all four bars of equal height, indicating consistent magnitude across all positions. In the “Decreasing” pattern, bar heights decline from left to right, with the tallest bar on the far left and the shortest on the far right. The “Spindle” pattern features a central peak, with the two middle bars being the tallest and the outermost bars being the shortest, creating a symmetrical, bell-like shape. The “Bottleneck” pattern displays a dip in the middle, with the first and last bars being taller than the two central bars, forming a U-shaped profile. Each pattern is labeled directly beneath its corresponding set of bars, and all bars are rendered in the same pale green color with no additional annotations, gridlines, or numerical values, suggesting the chart is intended to convey qualitative structural trends rather than precise quantitative measurements.
